bookInfo.name: New History of the Five Dynasties

title.zh: 卷十三 梁家人傳第一:
title.en: Volume 13: The Later Liang Imperial Family
title.raw: 卷十三 梁家人傳第一: Volume 13: The Later Liang Imperial Family

sentences.zh: 新五代史·傳嗚呼，梁之惡極矣！

translations.literal: New History of the Five Dynasties — Biographies. Alas, Liang’s wickedness reached the extreme!
translations.idiomatic: From the New History of the Five Dynasties, Biographies: Alas, how utterly vile the Liang were!

sentences.zh: 自其起盜賊，至於亡唐，其遺毒流於天下。

translations.literal: From their rise as bandits to their destruction of Tang, their lingering poison flowed through all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: From banditry to the overthrow of Tang, their taint spread across the realm.

sentences.zh: 天下豪傑，四面並起，孰不欲戡刃於胸，然卒不能少挫其鋒以得志。

translations.literal: Heroes throughout the realm rose on all sides; who did not wish to plunge a blade into their chest—yet in the end none could blunt their edge even slightly to fulfill their will.
translations.idiomatic: Champions rose on every quarter of the empire, each longing to drive a blade between their ribs; yet none could so much as nick their momentum or gain the upper hand.

sentences.zh: 梁之無敵於天下，可謂虎狼之強矣。

translations.literal: Liang’s being matchless under Heaven may be called the strength of tiger and wolf.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang were unmatched under Heaven—fierce as tigers and wolves.

sentences.zh: 及其敗也，因於一二女子之娛，至於洞胸流腸，刲若羊豕，禍生父子之間，乃知女色之能敗人矣。

translations.literal: When they fell, it was because of the pleasures of one or two women; it reached chests pierced and intestines spilled, carving like sheep and pigs, disaster born between father and son—then one knows how feminine beauty can ruin men.
translations.idiomatic: Their fall came through dalliance with a woman or two—chests gaping, guts spilled, bodies butchered like livestock, ruin erupting between father and son. Thus one learns how desire can undo a man.

sentences.zh: 自古女禍，大者亡天下，其次亡家，其次亡身，身茍免矣，猶及其子孫，雖遲速不回，未有無禍者也。

translations.literal: Since antiquity women’s calamity: in great cases it destroys the realm, next the family, next the person—even if the person escapes, it still reaches sons and grandsons; though swift or slow differ, none has been without disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Women’s curses since antiquity toppled empires first, households next, and lives after that; even when the man himself was spared, sons and grandsons still paid. Whether ruin came soon or late, no line escaped unscathed.

sentences.zh: 然原其本末，未始不起於忽微。

translations.literal: Yet tracing root and branch, none ever failed to begin from slight neglect.
translations.idiomatic: Trace any case to its roots, though, and it always began in trifling negligence.

sentences.zh: 《易·坤》之初六曰：「履霜，堅冰至。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes, Kun, first six lines, says: “Treading frost, hard ice arrives.”
translations.idiomatic: In the Book of Changes, the hexagram Kun, first line: “Frost underfoot means solid ice ahead.”

sentences.zh: 」《家人》之初九曰：「閑有家，悔亡。

translations.literal: ” The Family, first nine lines, says: “Regulating the household, regret vanishes.”
translations.idiomatic: ” In the Family, the first line: “Order in the household drives away regret.”

sentences.zh: 」其言至矣，可不戒哉！

translations.literal: ” Their words reach the utmost—how can one not be warned!
translations.idiomatic: ” The warning could not be plainer—who would not take heed!

sentences.zh: 梁之家事，《詩》所謂「不可道」者。

translations.literal: Liang’s household affairs are what the Odes call “unspeakable.”
translations.idiomatic: The Liang household was what the Book of Songs means by “things that must not be told.”

sentences.zh: 至於唐、晉以後，親疏嫡庶亂矣！

translations.literal: By Tang and Jin afterward, near and far, legitimate and secondary, were in chaos!
translations.idiomatic: After Tang and Jin, the lines between kin and stranger, principal wife and concubine, dissolved into chaos.

sentences.zh: 作《家人傳》。

translations.literal: [The author] composed “The Biography of the Imperial Family.”
translations.idiomatic: Hence this “Imperial Family” biography.

sentences.zh: 文惠皇后王氏

translations.literal: Empress Wenhuì, née Wang
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wenhuì, of the Wang clan

sentences.zh: 梁太祖母曰文惠皇后王氏，單州單父人也。

translations.literal: Liang Taizu’s mother was called Empress Wenhuì, surnamed Wang, a native of Shanfu in Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu of Liang’s mother, posthumously Empress Wenhuì, was a Wang of Shanfu in Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 其生三子：長曰廣王全昱，次曰朗王存，其次太祖。

translations.literal: She bore three sons: the eldest was called Prince of Guang Quanyu, the next Prince of Lang Cun, and the youngest Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: She bore three sons: Quanyu, Prince of Guang; Cun, Prince of Lang; and youngest of all, Taizu.

sentences.zh: 后少寡，攜其三子傭食蕭縣人劉崇家。

translations.literal: The empress was widowed young; she took her three sons to work for food at the home of Liu Chong of Xiao County.
translations.idiomatic: Widowed young, she hired out her three sons as laborers in the household of Liu Chong of Xiao County.

sentences.zh: 太祖壯而無賴，縣中皆厭苦之。

translations.literal: Taizu in his prime was a ruffian; the whole county detested and suffered him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu in his prime was a wastrel; the whole county loathed and endured him.

sentences.zh: 崇患太祖慵墮不作業，數加笞責，獨崇母憐之，時時自為櫛沐，戒家人曰：「朱三非常人也，宜善遇之！

translations.literal: Chong resented Taizu’s laziness and refusal to work, and often beat him with the rod; only Chong’s mother pitied him, now and then combing and washing him herself, warning the household: “Zhu the Third is no ordinary man—you should treat him well!”
translations.idiomatic: Chong hated Taizu’s idleness and beat him often; only Chong’s mother pitied him, bathing and combing his hair herself, and told the family: “Zhu the Third is no ordinary man—treat him kindly!”

sentences.zh: 」黃巢起，太祖與存俱亡為盜，從黃巢攻廣州，存戰死。

translations.literal: ” When Huang Chao rose, Taizu and Cun both fled to become bandits; following Huang Chao they attacked Guangzhou; Cun died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: ” When Huang Chao rebelled, Taizu and Cun both took to the hills; marching on Guangzhou under Chao, Cun was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 居數歲，太祖背巢降唐，反以破巢，遂鎮宣武。

translations.literal: After several years Taizu turned against Chao and surrendered to Tang, then in turn destroyed Chao, and thus held Xuanwu as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years Taizu deserted Chao for Tang, then turned and shattered Chao’s forces, and took the Xuanwu command.

sentences.zh: 乃遣人以車馬之蕭縣，迎后於崇家。

translations.literal: Then he sent men with chariots and horses to Xiao County to welcome the empress from Chong’s home.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent carriages and escorts to Xiao County to fetch the empress from the Chong household.

sentences.zh: 使者至門，后惶恐走避，謂劉氏曰：「朱三落魄無行，作賊死矣，何以至此邪！

translations.literal: When the envoy reached the gate the empress fled in alarm, saying to the Liu household: “Zhu the Third was down-and-out and lawless—he must have died a bandit’s death; what brings you here?”
translations.idiomatic: At the knock on the door the empress shrank back in terror and told the Lius: “Zhu the Third was a good-for-nothing who turned bandit—he must be dead. Why have you come?”

sentences.zh: 」使者具道太祖所以然，后乃驚喜泣下，與崇母俱載以歸，封晉國太夫人。

translations.literal: ” The envoy fully explained Taizu’s situation; the empress then wept in startled joy, and together with Chong’s mother rode back; she was enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: ” The envoy told the whole story; the empress wept for joy. She and Chong’s mother rode back together, and she was created Grand Lady of Jin.

sentences.zh: 太祖置酒太夫人前，舉觴為壽，歡甚。

translations.literal: Taizu set out wine before the Grand Lady, raised his goblet to wish her long life, and rejoiced greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu spread a feast before the Grand Lady, raised his cup to her long life, and made merry.

sentences.zh: 太祖啟曰：「朱五經平生讀書，不登一第，有子為節度使，無忝於先人也。

translations.literal: Taizu said: “Zhu the Fifth Classicist read books all his life and never passed the examinations; he has a son who is a military commissioner—no shame before our ancestors.”
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said: “Father Zhu the Classicist studied all his life yet never won a degree; he has a son who commands a circuit—he need not blush before the ancestors.”

sentences.zh: 」后惻然良久曰：「汝能至此，可謂英特，然行義未必得如先人也！

translations.literal: ” The empress was sorrowful a long while and said: “You have reached this point—one may call you exceptional—but your conduct and righteousness may not equal your forebears!”
translations.idiomatic: ” The empress was silent a long while, then said: “You have risen far—one might call you extraordinary—but your deeds may not match your father’s.”

sentences.zh: 」太祖莫知其故，后曰：「朱二與汝俱從黃巢，獨死蠻嶺，其孤皆在午溝，汝今富貴，獨不念之乎？

translations.literal: ” Taizu did not know her reason; the empress said: “Zhu the Second went with you to follow Huang Chao and alone died in the southern wilds; his orphans are all at Wugou—now that you are rich and noble, do you alone not think of them?”
translations.idiomatic: ” Taizu did not understand; the empress said: “Your brother Zhu the Second followed Huang Chao with you and died alone in the south; his children still live at Wugou—are you too grand now to remember them?”

sentences.zh: 」太祖泣涕謝罪，乃悉召存諸子以歸。

translations.literal: ” Taizu wept tears and begged forgiveness, then summoned all of Cun’s sons and brought them home.
translations.idiomatic: ” Taizu wept and begged pardon, then sent for all of Cun’s sons and brought them home.

sentences.zh: 太祖剛暴多殺戮，后每誡之，多賴以全活。

translations.literal: Taizu was harsh, violent, and much given to killing; the empress often admonished him, and many lives were spared through her.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was brutal and bloodthirsty; the empress often checked him, and many owed their lives to her.

sentences.zh: 大順二年秋，后疾，卜者曰：「宜還故鄉。

translations.literal: In autumn of the second year of Dazhun, the empress fell ill; the diviner said: “She should return to her native place.”
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Dazhun 2 the empress fell ill; augurs said she must go home.

sentences.zh: 」乃歸。

translations.literal: ” Then she returned.
translations.idiomatic: ” She went back.

sentences.zh: 卒於午溝。

translations.literal: She died at Wugou.
translations.idiomatic: She died at Wugou.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，立四廟，追尊皇考為穆皇帝，后曰文惠皇后。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne he established four ancestral temples, posthumously honoring his father as Emperor Mu and the empress as Empress Wenhuì.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu’s accession he founded four temples, raising his father to Emperor Mu and his mother to Empress Wenhuì.

sentences.zh: 元貞皇后張氏

translations.literal: Empress Yuanzhen, née Zhang
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yuanzhen, of the Zhang clan

sentences.zh: 太祖元貞皇后張氏，單州碭山縣渠亭里富家子也。

translations.literal: Taizu’s Empress Yuanzhen, surnamed Zhang, was the daughter of a wealthy family at Quetingli in Dangshan County, Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu’s Empress Yuanzhen was a Zhang of Quetingli in Dangshan, Shanzhou, born to a rich household.

sentences.zh: 太祖少以婦聘之，生末帝。

translations.literal: When Taizu was young he took her as wife by betrothal; she bore the Last Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu betrothed her in his youth; she bore Youzhen, the Last Emperor.

sentences.zh: 太祖貴，封魏國夫人。

translations.literal: When Taizu rose high, she was enfeoffed as Lady of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu’s star rose, she was created Lady of Wei.

sentences.zh: 后賢明精悍，動有禮法，雖太祖剛暴，亦嘗畏之。

translations.literal: The empress was worthy, bright, and sharp; in movement she had ritual propriety—even Taizu, though harsh and violent, sometimes feared her.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy, keen, and exact in deportment, she could awe even the brutal Taizu.

sentences.zh: 太祖每以外事訪之，后言多中。

translations.literal: Whenever Taizu consulted her on outside affairs, the empress’s words often hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: He often asked her counsel on state matters, and she was usually right.

sentences.zh: 太祖時時暴怒殺戮，后嘗救護，人賴以獲全。

translations.literal: Taizu was at times violently angry and killed; the empress often rescued people, and many owed their survival to her.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu raged and killed, she often intervened; many lived because of her.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗出兵，行至中途，后意以為不然，馳一介召之，如期而至。

translations.literal: Once when Taizu was marching out and had gone halfway, the empress thought it wrong and sent a single messenger to summon him; he returned on the appointed day.
translations.idiomatic: Once Taizu had marched halfway on campaign when the empress decided the move was wrong and sent a lone rider to call him back; he returned on the day she named.

sentences.zh: 郴王友裕攻徐州，破朱瑾於石佛山，瑾走，友裕不追，太祖大怒，奪其兵。

translations.literal: Prince of Chen Youyu attacked Xuzhou and defeated Zhu Jin at Stone Buddha Mountain; Jin fled, but Youyu did not pursue. Taizu was furious and stripped him of his command.
translations.idiomatic: Youyu, Prince of Chen, besieged Xuzhou and routed Zhu Jin at Stone Buddha Mountain; Jin escaped, but Youyu let him go. Taizu raged and relieved him of command.

sentences.zh: 友裕惶恐，與數騎亡山中，久之，自匿於廣王。

translations.literal: Youyu was fearful; with several horsemen he fled into the mountains, and after a long while hid himself with the Prince of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Youyu fled into the hills with a few riders and, after long hiding, took refuge with the Prince of Guang.

sentences.zh: 后陰使人教友裕脫身自歸，友裕晨馳入見太祖，拜伏庭中，泣涕請死，太祖怒甚，使左右捽出，將斬之。

translations.literal: The empress secretly sent someone to teach Youyu how to slip free and return of himself; at dawn Youyu galloped in to see Taizu, prostrated himself in the courtyard, wept and begged death; Taizu was very angry and had attendants drag him out to be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The empress secretly coached Youyu to give himself up; at dawn he rode in, threw himself on the courtyard stones, wept, and asked to die. Taizu ordered him dragged out for execution.

sentences.zh: 后聞之，不及履，走庭中持友裕泣曰：「汝束身歸罪，豈不欲明非反乎？

translations.literal: Hearing this, the empress, without time to put on shoes, ran into the courtyard, held Youyu, and wept: “You bound yourself and came back to answer the charge—did you not mean to show you were no rebel?”
translations.idiomatic: The empress heard, ran barefoot into the yard, clutched Youyu, and wept: “You came back in bonds to clear yourself—was that not proof you never rebelled?”

sentences.zh: 」太祖意解，乃免。

translations.literal: ” Taizu’s mind eased, and he pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Taizu relented and spared him.

sentences.zh: 太祖已破朱瑾，納其妻以歸，后迎太祖於封丘，太祖告之。

translations.literal: After Taizu had defeated Zhu Jin and taken his wife home, the empress met Taizu at Fengqiu and he told her.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu broke Zhu Jin and brought Jin’s wife away, the empress met him at Fengqiu and he told her what he had done.

sentences.zh: 后遽見瑾妻，瑾妻再拜，后亦拜，淒然泣下曰：「兗鄆與司空同姓之國，昆仲之間，以小故興干戈，而使吾姒至此；

translations.literal: The empress hurried to see Jin’s wife; Jin’s wife bowed twice, the empress also bowed, and said tearfully: “Yan and Yun are states of the same surname as the Director of Works; between brothers a small quarrel raised arms, and brought my sister-in-law to this—
translations.idiomatic: The empress went straight to Jin’s wife; Jin’s wife bowed low, and the empress bowed in return, weeping: “Yan and Yun share our house’s surname; brothers drew swords over a trifle, and your plight could have been mine—

sentences.zh: 若不幸汴州失守，妾亦如此矣！

translations.literal: if by misfortune Bianzhou were lost, your servant too would be like this!”
translations.idiomatic: had Bianzhou fallen, I would stand where you stand today!”

sentences.zh: 」言已又泣。

translations.literal: Having spoken, she wept again.
translations.idiomatic: She wept again when she had finished.

sentences.zh: 太祖為之感動，乃送瑾妻為尼，后嘗給其衣食。

translations.literal: Taizu was moved by this and sent Jin’s wife to become a nun; the empress often supplied her food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was touched and had Jin’s wife tonsured; the empress often sent her food and clothes.

sentences.zh: 司空，太祖時檢校官也。

translations.literal: “Director of Works” was Taizu’s honorary title at the time.
translations.idiomatic: “Director of Works” was the honorary post Taizu then held.

sentences.zh: 天祐元年，后以疾卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianyou the empress died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou 1 the empress died of illness.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，追冊為賢妃。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne he posthumously enfeoffed her as Worthy Consort.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizu’s accession she was posthumously created Worthy Consort.

sentences.zh: 初葬開封縣潤色鄉，末帝立，追謚曰元貞皇太后，祔於宣陵。

translations.literal: At first she was buried in Runse Township, Kaifeng County; when the Last Emperor took the throne he posthumously honored her as Empress Dowager Yuanzhen and enshrined her at Xuanling.
translations.idiomatic: She was first buried at Runse in Kaifeng; the Last Emperor later gave her the posthumous title Empress Dowager Yuanzhen and placed her tablet in Xuanling.

sentences.zh: 后已死，太祖始為荒淫，卒以及禍云。

translations.literal: After the empress died Taizu first became dissolute and wanton, and in the end met disaster—so it is said.
translations.idiomatic: After her death Taizu turned to debauchery, and disaster followed—or so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 陳昭儀

translations.literal: Honored Consort Chen
translations.idiomatic: Honored Consort Chen

sentences.zh: 昭儀陳氏，宋州人也，少以色進。

translations.literal: Honored Consort Chen was a native of Songzhou; in youth she entered through beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Honored Consort Chen came from Songzhou and entered the palace for her looks.

sentences.zh: 太祖已貴，嬪妾數百，而昭儀專寵。

translations.literal: After Taizu rose high, his concubines numbered in the hundreds, yet the Honored Consort alone held his favor.
translations.idiomatic: Though Taizu kept hundreds of women once he was great, the Honored Consort alone held his heart.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗疾，昭儀與尼數十人晝夜為佛法，未嘗少懈，太祖以為愛己，尤寵之。

translations.literal: Once when Taizu fell ill, the Honored Consort with several dozen nuns performed Buddhist rites day and night without the least slackening; Taizu thought this love for himself and favored her all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu fell ill she and dozens of nuns kept Buddhist observances night and day without rest; he took it as devotion to him and doted on her the more.

sentences.zh: 開平三年，度為尼，居宋州佛寺。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaiping she was ordained a nun and lived in a Songzhou monastery.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping 3 she took the tonsure and retired to a monastery in Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 李昭容

translations.literal: Honored Lady Li
translations.idiomatic: Honored Lady Li

sentences.zh: 昭容李氏，亦以色進。

translations.literal: Honored Lady Li also entered through beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Honored Lady Li, too, had risen by her beauty.

sentences.zh: 尤謹願，未嘗去左右。

translations.literal: She was especially careful and dutiful and never left his side.
translations.idiomatic: She was modest and steadfast and rarely left his side.

sentences.zh: 太祖病，晝寢方寐，忽棟折，獨李氏侍側，遽牽太祖衣，太祖驚走，棟折寢上，太祖德之，拜昭容。

translations.literal: When Taizu was ill he napped by day and had just fallen asleep when suddenly a ridgepole broke; only Lady Li attended at his side; she quickly pulled Taizu’s garment; Taizu fled in alarm; the beam fell on the couch; Taizu was grateful and enfeoffed her as Honored Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Once, as Taizu dozed in illness, a roof beam snapped; only Lady Li was beside him. She seized his robe; he scrambled clear as the timber crashed on the couch. Grateful, he created her Honored Lady.

sentences.zh: 皆不知其所終。

translations.literal: None know how any of them ended.
translations.idiomatic: None of their final fates are recorded.

sentences.zh: 末帝德妃張氏

translations.literal: Last Emperor’s Virtuous Consort Zhang
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Consort Zhang of the Last Emperor

sentences.zh: 末帝德妃張氏，其父歸霸，事太祖為梁功臣。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor’s Virtuous Consort Zhang—her father Guiba served Taizu and was a meritorious minister of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor’s Virtuous Consort Zhang was daughter of Guiba, a Liang minister who had served Taizu with distinction.

sentences.zh: 帝為王時，以婦聘之。

translations.literal: When the emperor was still a prince he took her as wife by betrothal.
translations.idiomatic: While still heir, he betrothed her.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，將冊妃為后，妃請待帝郊天，而帝卒不得郊。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne he was about to install the consort as empress; the consort asked to wait until he sacrificed to Heaven at the suburban altar, but the emperor in the end never performed that rite.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession he meant to make her empress; she asked to wait until he had worshipped Heaven at the suburban altar, but he never held that ceremony.

sentences.zh: 貞明五年，妃病甚，帝遽冊為德妃，其夕薨，年二十四。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenming the consort fell gravely ill; the emperor hastily created her Virtuous Consort; that very night she died, aged twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming 5 she fell mortally ill; the emperor rushed her creation as Virtuous Consort, and she died that night at twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 次妃郭氏

translations.literal: Second Consort Guo
translations.idiomatic: Second Consort Guo

sentences.zh: 次妃郭氏，父歸厚，事梁為登州刺史。

translations.literal: Second Consort Guo—her father Guihou served Liang as prefect of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Second Consort Guo’s father Guihou had been prefect of Dengzhou under Liang.

sentences.zh: 妃少以色進。

translations.literal: The consort in youth entered through beauty.
translations.idiomatic: She, too, had entered the palace young for her looks.

sentences.zh: 梁亡，唐莊宗入汴，梁故妃妾，皆號泣迎拜。

translations.literal: When Liang fell, Zhuangzong entered Bian; Liang’s former consorts all wailed and came forward to bow.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang fell and Zhuangzong took Bian, the former Liang women came weeping to bow before him.

sentences.zh: 賀王友雍妃石氏有色，莊宗召之，石氏慢罵，莊宗殺之。

translations.literal: Prince of He Youyong’s consort Lady Shi was beautiful; Zhuangzong summoned her; Lady Shi reviled him slowly; Zhuangzong killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Youyong, Prince of He, had a beautiful consort, Lady Shi; Zhuangzong called for her, and she cursed him to his face. He had her killed.

sentences.zh: 次以召妃，妃懼而聽命。

translations.literal: Next he summoned the consort; the consort feared him and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was summoned next; afraid, she obeyed.

sentences.zh: 已而度為尼，賜名誓正，居於洛陽。

translations.literal: Before long she was ordained a nun, given the religious name Shizheng, and lived in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: She was soon tonsured, given the dharma name Shizheng, and settled in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 初，莊宗之入汴也，末帝登建國樓，謂控鶴指揮使皇甫麟曰：「吾，晉世仇也，不可俟彼刀鋸，卿可盡我命，無使我落仇人之手！

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhuangzong entered Bian, the Last Emperor ascended the Jianguo Tower and said to Control Crane Commandant Huangfu Lin: “I am Jin’s hereditary foe; I cannot wait for their blades—do you end my life so I do not fall into the enemy’s hands!”
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong first entered Bian, the Last Emperor climbed the Jianguo Tower and told Huangfu Lin, commander of the Control Crane Guard: “Jin is my hereditary enemy. I will not wait for their steel—finish me, so I never fall into their hands!”

sentences.zh: 麟與帝相持慟哭。

translations.literal: Lin and the emperor clung to each other and wept in anguish.
translations.idiomatic: Lin and the emperor embraced and wept.

sentences.zh: 是夕，進刃於帝，麟亦自剄。

translations.literal: That night he advanced a blade to the emperor; Lin also cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: That night Lin drove the blade home; then he cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入汴，命河南張全義葬其屍，藏其首於太社。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong entered Bian and ordered Zhang Quanyi of Henan to bury the corpse and store the head in the Grand Temple of Soil and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong entered Bian and ordered Zhang Quanyi of Henan to bury the body and keep the head in the state altar.

sentences.zh: 晉天福三年，詔太社先藏罪人首級，許親屬收葬，乃出末帝首，遣右衛將軍安崇阮與妃同葬之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianfu of Jin an edict said that heads of criminals long kept in the Grand Temple might be reclaimed by kin for burial; the Last Emperor’s head was then taken out, and Right Palace Gate General An Chongruan was sent to bury it together with the consort.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Tianfu 3 an edict allowed families to reclaim criminal heads held at the altar; the Last Emperor’s head was released, and Right Palace Gate General An Chongruan buried it with the consort.

sentences.zh: 妃卒洛陽。

translations.literal: The consort died in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The consort died in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 太祖兄子

translations.literal: Taizu’s elder brother’s sons
translations.idiomatic: Sons of Taizu’s elder brothers

sentences.zh: 太祖二兄：曰全昱，曰存。

translations.literal: Taizu’s two elder brothers: one called Quanyu, one called Cun.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had two elder brothers: Quanyu and Cun.

sentences.zh: 八子：長曰友裕，次曰友珪、友璋、友貞、友雍、友徽、友孜，其一養子曰友文。

translations.literal: Eight sons: the eldest Youyu, next Yougui, Youzhang, Youzhen, Youyong, Youhui, Youzi, and one adopted son Youwen.
translations.idiomatic: Eight sons by blood: Youyu, then Yougui, Youzhang, Youzhen, Youyong, Youhui, and Youzi, plus the adopted Youwen.

sentences.zh: 開平元年五月乙酉，封友文為博王、友珪郢王、友璋福王、友貞均王、友雍賀王、友徽建王。

translations.literal: On yiyou in the fifth month of the first year of Kaiping, Youwen was enfeoffed Prince of Bo, Yougui Prince of Ying, Youzhang Prince of Fu, Youzhen Prince of Jun, Youyong Prince of He, and Youhui Prince of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou in the fifth month of Kaiping 1, Youwen became Prince of Bo, Yougui of Ying, Youzhang of Fu, Youzhen of Jun, Youyong of He, and Youhui of Jian.

sentences.zh: 友裕前即位卒，追封郴王，而康王友孜，末帝即位封。

translations.literal: Youyu had died before the enthronement and was posthumously created Prince of Chen; Prince of Kang Youzi was enfeoffed when the Last Emperor took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Youyu had died before the accession and was posthumously made Prince of Chen; Youzi, Prince of Kang, received his title under the Last Emperor.

sentences.zh: 友璋初為壽州團練使、押左右番殿直、監豐德庫，友珪時，為鄆州留後，末帝時，為忠武軍節度使，徙鎮武寧，及友雍、友徽皆不知其所終。

translations.literal: Youzhang at first was prefect of Shouzhou and superintendent of the Left and Right Palace Guards and overseer of the Fengde treasury; under Yougui he was military governor of Yan; under the Last Emperor he was military governor of Zhongwu, then transferred to command Wuning; as for Youyong and Youhui, none know how they ended.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhang first held Shouzhou, the palace guard commands, and the Fengde treasury; under Yougui he governed Yan; under the Last Emperor he held Zhongwu, then Wuning. The fates of Youyong and Youhui are unknown.

sentences.zh: 兄廣王全昱

translations.literal: Elder brother, Prince of Guang Quanyu
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother: Quanyu, Prince of Guang

sentences.zh: （全昱子友諒 友能 友誨）〉

translations.literal: (Sons of Quanyu: Youliang, Youneng, Youhui)
translations.idiomatic: (Sons of Quanyu: Youliang, Youneng, Youhui)

sentences.zh: 廣王全昱，太祖即位封。

translations.literal: Prince of Guang Quanyu was enfeoffed when Taizu took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyu, Prince of Guang, was created when Taizu took the throne.

sentences.zh: 太祖與仲兄存俱亡為盜，全昱獨與其母猶寄食劉崇家。

translations.literal: Taizu and his second brother Cun both fled to become bandits; Quanyu alone remained with their mother still working for food at Liu Chong’s home.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu and the middle brother Cun had both turned bandit; Quanyu alone stayed with their mother, still laboring in Liu Chong’s house.

sentences.zh: 太祖已貴，乃與其母俱歸宣武，領嶺南西道節度使。

translations.literal: After Taizu rose high, mother and son together returned to Xuanwu; he held the post of military governor of Lingnan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu prospered, mother and son came to Xuanwu; Quanyu held the Lingnan West military governorship.

sentences.zh: 以太師致仕。

translations.literal: He retired on the honorary title of Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He retired with the honorary rank of Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 太祖將受禪，有司備禮前殿，全昱視之，顧太祖曰：「朱三，爾作得否？

translations.literal: When Taizu was about to receive the abdication, the offices prepared the rites in the front hall; Quanyu looked on and, turning to Taizu, said: “Zhu the Third, can you pull this off?”
translations.idiomatic: As Taizu prepared to accept the throne, the ritual officers set the ceremony in the front hall; Quanyu watched and asked him: “Zhu the Third—do you really think you can manage this?”

sentences.zh: 」太祖宴居宮中，與王飲博，全昱酒酣，取骰子擊盆而迸之，呼太祖曰：「朱三，爾碭山一百姓，遭逢天子用汝為四鎮節度使，於汝何負？

translations.literal: ” When Taizu was at leisure in the palace drinking and gambling with the prince, Quanyu, wine-flushed, took dice and struck the basin so they flew out, calling to Taizu: “Zhu the Third, you were a common man of Dangshan—by heaven’s favor you became military commissioner of four circuits; what did they owe you?”?
translations.idiomatic: ” Once, as Taizu drank and diced with him in the palace, Quanyu, deep in wine, hurled the dice against the bowl and shouted: “Zhu the Third, you were a dirt farmer from Dangshan until heaven made you lord of four circuits—what did the throne ever owe you?”?

sentences.zh: 而滅他唐家三百年社稷，吾將見汝赤其族矣，安用博為！

translations.literal: yet you destroyed another’s Tang altars of three hundred years— I will live to see your clan exterminated to the last man; what use is gambling!
translations.idiomatic: and you wiped out Tang’s three-century throne—I will see your whole line butchered. What are you dicing for!

sentences.zh: 」太祖不悅，罷會。

translations.literal: ” Taizu was displeased and dismissed the gathering.
translations.idiomatic: ” Taizu took offense and broke up the party.

sentences.zh: 全昱亦不樂在京師，常居碭山故里。

translations.literal: Quanyu also took no pleasure in the capital and usually lived in his old home in Dangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyu disliked the capital as well and mostly stayed in his native Dangshan.

sentences.zh: 三子皆封王：友諒衡王，友能惠王，友誨邵王。

translations.literal: All three sons were enfeoffed as kings: Youliang as Prince of Heng, Youneng as Prince of Hui, and Youhui as Prince of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the three sons received a royal title: Youliang as Prince of Heng, Youneng as Prince of Hui, and Youhui as Prince of Shao.

sentences.zh: 友能為宋、滑二州留後、陳州刺史，所至為不法，奸人多依倚之。

translations.literal: Youneng was acting governor of Song and Hua prefectures and prefect of Chen; wherever he went he broke the law, and many villains relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Youneng served as acting governor of Song and Hua and as prefect of Chen, ruling lawlessly wherever he was posted; rogues flocked to his patronage.

sentences.zh: 而陳俗好淫祠左道，其學佛者，自立一法，號曰「上乘」，晝夜伏聚，男女雜亂。

translations.literal: Chen custom favored heterodox shrines and left-hand ways; among those who studied Buddhism they established their own law, called the “Supreme Vehicle,” gathering day and night in secret, men and women mingling in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chen were fond of illicit cults; some Buddhists formed a sect called the “Supreme Vehicle,” meeting by night with men and women intermingled in debauchery.

sentences.zh: 妖人母乙、董乙聚眾稱天子，建置官屬，友能初縱之，乙等攻劫州縣，末帝發兵擊滅之。

translations.literal: Sorcerers Mu Yi and Dong Yi gathered crowds and styled themselves emperors, setting up officials; at first Youneng indulged them; when Yi and the rest raided prefectures and counties, the Last Emperor sent troops and destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: The wonder-workers Mu Yi and Dong Yi raised followers, crowned themselves, and appointed a court; Youneng at first let them run wild. When they began sacking the countryside, the Last Emperor sent an army and exterminated them.

sentences.zh: 自康王友孜謀反伏誅，末帝始疏斥宗室，宗室皆反仄。

translations.literal: From the time Youzi, Prince of Kang, plotted rebellion and was executed, the Last Emperor began to keep the imperial clan at a distance; the clan grew cramped and uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: After Youzi, Prince of Kang, was caught in treason and put to death, the Last Emperor turned against his kinsmen, and the whole clan lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 貞明四年，友能以陳州兵反，犯京師，至陳留，兵敗，還走陳州，後數月降，末帝赦之，降為房陵侯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenming, Youneng rebelled with Chen troops and marched on the capital; at Chenliu his army was broken; he fled back to Chen; months later he surrendered; the Last Emperor pardoned him and reduced him to Marquis of Fangling.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming 4, Youneng rose in Chenzhou and struck toward the capital. Defeated at Chenliu, he fled home; after some months he submitted. The Last Emperor spared his life but stripped him to Marquis of Fangling.

sentences.zh: 友誨為陜州節度使，欲以州兵為亂，末帝召還京師，與友諒、友能皆被幽囚。

translations.literal: Youhui was military governor of Shaan; he wished to raise the prefectural army in revolt; the Last Emperor summoned him back to the capital, and he, with Youliang and Youneng, were all imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Youhui governed Shaan and planned to mutiny with his garrison. The Last Emperor recalled him to the capital; he and Youliang and Youneng were thrown into confinement.

sentences.zh: 梁亡，莊宗入汴，皆見殺。

translations.literal: When Liang fell, Zhuangzong entered Bian; all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang fell and Zhuangzong took Bian, all were put to death.

sentences.zh: ○兄朗王存

translations.literal: ○ Elder brother, Prince of Lang Cun
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother: Cun, Prince of Lang

sentences.zh: （存子友寧友倫）〉

translations.literal: (Sons of Cun: Youning and Youlun)
translations.idiomatic: (Sons of Cun: Youning and Youlun)

sentences.zh: 朗王存，初與太祖俱從黃巢攻廣州，存戰死。

translations.literal: Prince of Lang Cun had at first marched with Taizu under Huang Chao to attack Guangzhou; Cun died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Cun, Prince of Lang, had marched with Taizu under Huang Chao against Guangzhou and was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 存子友寧、友倫。

translations.literal: Cun’s sons were Youning and Youlun.
translations.idiomatic: Cun left two sons: Youning and Youlun.

sentences.zh: 友寧字安仁，幼聰敏，喜慍不形於色。

translations.literal: Youning, courtesy name Anren, was clever as a child; joy and anger never showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Youning, styled Anren, was bright from boyhood and never let pleasure or wrath show on his face.

sentences.zh: 太祖以為軍校，善用弓劍。

translations.literal: Taizu made him an army officer; he was skilled with bow and sword.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu appointed him to the army; he excelled with bow and blade.

sentences.zh: 遷衙內制勝都指揮使、龔州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to commander of the Inner Palace Victorious Command and prefect of Gongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to command the Inner Palace Victorious Guard and to govern Gongzhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖圍鳳翔，遣友寧東備宣武。

translations.literal: When Taizu besieged Fengxiang, he sent Youning east to guard Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: While Taizu besieged Fengxiang, he sent Youning east to hold Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 王師範襲梁，圍齊州，友寧引兵擊之，奪馬千匹，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: Wang Shifan attacked Liang and besieged Qizhou; Youning led troops against him, seized a thousand horses, and severed heads by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shifan struck Liang and invested Qizhou; Youning met him, captured a thousand horses, and took thousands of heads.

sentences.zh: 太祖奉昭宗還京師，拜友寧建武軍節度使，賜號「迎鑾毅勇功臣」。

translations.literal: When Taizu escorted Emperor Zhaozong back to the capital, he enfeoffed Youning as military governor of Jianwu and bestowed the title “Valiant Merit Lord Who Welcomes the Imperial Carriage.”
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu brought Emperor Zhaozong home, he made Youning military governor of Jianwu and gave him the honorific “Valiant Merit Lord Who Welcomes the Imperial Carriage.”

sentences.zh: 太祖復遣攻師範，圍博昌，屠之，清河為之不流。

translations.literal: Taizu again sent him against Shifan; he besieged Bochang and slaughtered it, and the Qing River would not flow.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent him against Shifan again; he invested Bochang and massacred the city until the Qing River ran with blood and would not flow.

sentences.zh: 戰於石樓，兵敗，友寧墮馬見殺。

translations.literal: In battle at Shilou his army was defeated; Youning fell from his horse and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: At Shilou his force was routed; Youning was thrown from his horse and slain.

sentences.zh: 友倫幼亦明敏，通《論語》、小學，曉音律。

translations.literal: Youlun as a child was also bright; he mastered the Analects and the Elementary Learning and understood musical pitch.
translations.idiomatic: Youlun too was precocious; he knew the Analects and the Elementary Learning and understood pitch and mode.

sentences.zh: 存已死，太祖以友倫為元從馬軍指揮使，表右威武將軍。

translations.literal: Cun was already dead; Taizu made Youlun commander of the original-follower Horse Army and memorialized him as Right Mighty Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: With Cun dead, Taizu made Youlun commander of the veteran Horse Army and had him appointed Right Mighty Martial General.

sentences.zh: 燕人攻魏內黃，友倫以前鋒夜渡河，奪馬千匹。

translations.literal: When Yan forces attacked Neihuang in Wei, Youlun as vanguard crossed the river by night and seized a thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan troops struck Neihuang in Wei, Youlun led the van, forded the river by night, and took a thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 李罕之以潞州降梁，晉人攻潞，友倫以兵入潞州，取罕之以歸。

translations.literal: When Li Hanzhi surrendered Luzhou to Liang and Jin attacked Luzhou, Youlun entered Luzhou with troops and brought Hanzhi back.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hanzhi surrendered Luzhou to Liang; when Jin besieged it, Youlun marched in, lifted the siege, and escorted Hanzhi home.

sentences.zh: 累遷檢校司空，領藤州刺史。

translations.literal: By repeated promotion he reached honorary Sikong and held the prefecture of Teng.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to honorary Sikong and governed Tengzhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖圍鳳翔，晉人襲梁，友倫以兵三萬至{樊石}山，晉人乃卻，友倫西會太祖於鳳翔。

translations.literal: When Taizu besieged Fengxiang and Jin raided Liang, Youlun came with thirty thousand men to Mount {Fan-Shi}; Jin then withdrew, and Youlun went west to join Taizu at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: While Taizu invested Fengxiang, Jin struck Liang; Youlun brought thirty thousand men to Mount Fanshi and drove them back, then marched west to Taizu at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 昭宗還長安，拜友倫寧遠軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong returned to Chang’an, he appointed Youlun military governor of Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong went back to Chang’an, Youlun was made military governor of Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 太祖東歸，留友倫宿衛，伺察昭宗所為。

translations.literal: When Taizu returned east, he left Youlun on palace guard duty to watch what Zhaozong did.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu left for the east and stationed Youlun in the palace to spy on the emperor’s every move.

sentences.zh: 友倫擊鞠墜馬死，太祖大怒，以兵七萬至河中。

translations.literal: Youlun died when he fell from his horse playing cuju; Taizu was furious and marched with seventy thousand men to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Youlun died in a polo fall; Taizu flew into a rage and marched seventy thousand men on Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 昭宗涕泣，不知所為，將奔太原，不果。

translations.literal: Zhaozong wept and knew not what to do; he was about to flee to Taiyuan but could not carry it through.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong wept in despair; he meant to flee to Taiyuan but never managed it.

sentences.zh: 宰相崔胤遣人止太祖，太祖以為友倫胤等殺之，奏請誅胤等，昭宗未從，乃遣友諒至京師，以兵圍開化坊，殺胤及京兆尹鄭元規、皇城使王建勛、飛龍使陳班、閣門使王建襲、客省使王建乂、前左僕射張浚。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Cui Yin sent men to stop Taizu; Taizu believed Youlun had been killed by Yin and the rest, memorialized asking that Yin be executed, and Zhaozong did not consent; Taizu then sent Youliang to the capital; with troops he surrounded Kaihua Ward and killed Yin, Henan prefect Zheng Yuangui, Imperial City Commissioner Wang Jianxun, Flying Dragon Commissioner Chen Ban, Gate Commissioner Wang Jianxi, Reception Commissioner Wang Jianyi, and former Left Vice Director Zhang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin sent envoys to halt him, but Taizu was convinced that Yin and his circle had murdered Youlun. He demanded their deaths; Zhaozong refused. Taizu then sent Youliang to the capital with troops, invested Kaihua Ward, and killed Yin, Zheng Yuangui of Henan, Wang Jianxun of the Imperial City, Chen Ban of the Flying Dragon Office, Wang Jianxi of the Gate Office, Wang Jianyi of the Reception Office, and the former Left Vice Director Zhang Jun.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，已封宗室，中書上議，故皇兄存，皇侄建武軍節度使友寧、寧遠軍節度使友倫，皆當封。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne he had already enfeoffed the clan; the Secretariat debated: the late elder brother Cun and the nephews, Jianwu military governor Youning and Ningyuan military governor Youlun, all ought to receive titles.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu’s accession the clan was already ennobled, but the Secretariat argued that his late brother Cun and his nephews Youning of Jianwu and Youlun of Ningyuan still deserved titles.

sentences.zh: 於是追封存朗王、友寧安王、友倫密王。

translations.literal: Thereupon Cun was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Lang, Youning Prince of An, and Youlun Prince of Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Cun was posthumously made Prince of Lang, Youning Prince of An, and Youlun Prince of Mi.

sentences.zh: 子郴王友裕

translations.literal: Son: Youyu, Prince of Chen
translations.idiomatic: Son: Youyu, Prince of Chen

sentences.zh: 冬，友裕取濮州，遂圍時溥於徐州。

translations.literal: In winter, Youyu took Puzhou, then besieged Shi Pu at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Youyu seized Puzhou and then invested Shi Pu in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 朱瑾以兵二萬救溥，友裕敗瑾於石佛山，瑾走。

translations.literal: Zhu Jin came with twenty thousand men to rescue Pu; Youyu defeated Jin at Mount Shifo, and Jin fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jin marched with twenty thousand to relieve Pu; Youyu routed him at Mount Shifo and Jin fled.

sentences.zh: 都虞候朱友恭讒之太祖，以為瑾可追而友裕不追。

translations.literal: Chief registrar Zhu Yougong slandered him to Taizu, saying Jin could have been pursued but Youyu did not pursue.
translations.idiomatic: The chief registrar Zhu Yougong whispered to Taizu that Jin could have been run down and that Youyu had let him escape.

sentences.zh: 太祖大怒，奪其兵屬龐師古，以友裕屬吏，使者誤致書於友裕，友裕惶恐，不知所為，賴張皇后教之，得免。

translations.literal: Taizu was furious, stripped Youyu of his troops and gave them to Pang Shigu, and handed Youyu over to the judicial officers; a messenger mistakenly delivered the writ to Youyu; Youyu was terrified and knew not what to do; he was spared thanks to Empress Zhang’s counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu raged, transferred Youyu’s command to Pang Shigu, and handed him to the law officers. A courier by mistake delivered the order to Youyu himself; in terror he knew not what to do, but Empress Zhang coached him and he escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 權知許州。

translations.literal: He acted as prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 許州近蔡，苦於大寇，居民殘破，友裕招撫流散，增戶三萬餘。

translations.literal: Xuzhou lay near Cai and had suffered great bandit raids; the people were broken; Youyu gathered the scattered and increased households by more than thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou bordered Cai and had been ravaged by raiders; the population was shattered. Youyu brought back refugees and added more than thirty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 遷諸軍都指揮使，與平兗、鄆，還領許州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to commander of all armies; with that force he pacified Yan and Yun, then returned to hold Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to commander of all armies, he helped subdue Yan and Yun and then resumed command at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 崔洪奔淮南，友裕引兵定蔡州，市不易肆。

translations.literal: When Cui Hong fled to Huainan, Youyu led troops to settle Caizhou, and the markets did not close.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Hong fled to Huainan, Youyu marched in and pacified Caizhou without disturbing trade.

sentences.zh: 太祖兼鎮護國軍，以友裕為留後。

translations.literal: When Taizu also held the Huguo command, he made Youyu acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took Huguo as well, he left Youyu as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 遷忠武軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to military governor of Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military governor of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 太祖攻鳳翔，未下，去攻邠州。

translations.literal: When Taizu attacked Fengxiang and could not take it, he left to attack Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu invested Fengxiang without success and turned to attack Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 友裕破靈臺、良原，下隴州，楊崇本以邠州降。

translations.literal: Youyu broke Lingtai and Liangyuan, took Longzhou, and Yang Chongben surrendered Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Youyu stormed Lingtai and Liangyuan, seized Longzhou, and Yang Chongben surrendered Bin.

sentences.zh: 後崇本復叛，太祖遣友裕攻之，屯於永壽。

translations.literal: Later Chongben rebelled again; Taizu sent Youyu against him, and he encamped at Yongshou.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongben rebelled again, Taizu sent Youyu against him; he camped at Yongshou.

sentences.zh: 友裕以疾卒。

translations.literal: Youyu died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Youyu died of illness.

sentences.zh: 子博王友文

translations.literal: Son: Youwen, Prince of Bo
translations.idiomatic: Son: Youwen, Prince of Bo

sentences.zh: 博王友文，字德明，本姓康名勤。

translations.literal: Youwen, courtesy name Deming, was originally surnamed Kang and named Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen, styled Deming, had been born Kang Qin.

sentences.zh: 幼美風姿，好學，善談論，頗能為詩，太祖養以為子。

translations.literal: As a boy he was handsome, loved learning, was skilled in discourse, and could write poetry; Taizu raised him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome and bookish as a youth, eloquent and able to write verse, he was adopted and raised by Taizu.

sentences.zh: 太祖領四鎮，以友文為度支鹽鐵制置使。

translations.literal: When Taizu held four commands, he made Youwen commissioner for revenue, salt, and iron.
translations.idiomatic: While Taizu governed four circuits, he made Youwen commissioner of revenue, salt, and iron.

sentences.zh: 太祖用兵四方，友文征賦聚斂以供軍實。

translations.literal: As Taizu waged war on all sides, Youwen levied and gathered taxes to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: While Taizu campaigned everywhere, Youwen levied taxes to fill the war chest.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，以故所領宣武、宣義、天平、護國四鎮征賦，置建昌宮總之，以友文為使，封博王。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, the levies of the four commands he had once held—Xuanwu, Xuanyi, Tianping, and Huguo—were placed under the Jianchang Palace for overall management, with Youwen as its director; he was enfeoffed Prince of Bo.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding he pooled the taxes of Xuanwu, Xuanyi, Tianping, and Huguo—the four commands he had held—under the Jianchang Palace with Youwen as director, and created him Prince of Bo.

sentences.zh: 太祖幸西都，友文留守東京。

translations.literal: When Taizu visited the western capital, Youwen remained to guard the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu went west, Youwen stayed behind as guardian of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 子庶人友珪

translations.literal: Son: Yougui the Deposed
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yougui, later the Deposed

sentences.zh: 太祖素剛暴，既病，而喜怒難測，是時左降者，必有後命，友珪大懼。

translations.literal: Taizu had always been fierce and violent; once ill, his joy and anger were hard to predict; at that time anyone demoted was sure to face a further order; Yougui was terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had always been brutal; in illness his moods were unpredictable, and a demotion now always meant worse to come. Yougui was terrified.

sentences.zh: 其妻張氏曰：「官家以傳國寶與王氏，使如東都召友文，君今受禍矣！

translations.literal: His wife, Lady Zhang, said: “His Majesty has given the seal of state to Lady Wang and sent her to the eastern capital to summon Youwen—you are about to suffer!
translations.idiomatic: His wife Zhang said: “The emperor has given the imperial seal to Lady Wang and sent her east to call Youwen home—you are finished!

sentences.zh: 」夫婦相對而泣。

translations.literal: ” Husband and wife faced each other and wept.
translations.idiomatic: ” Husband and wife wept face to face.

sentences.zh: 左右勸友珪曰：「事急計生，何不早自為圖？

translations.literal: Those about him urged Yougui: “When matters are urgent one must plan for life—why not act for yourself at once?
translations.idiomatic: His attendants urged him: “Desperate times call for desperate measures—why not strike first?

sentences.zh: 」友珪乃易衣服，微行入左龍虎軍，見統軍韓計事，以牙兵五百隨友珪，雜控鶴衛士而入。

translations.literal: ” Yougui then changed clothes, went in secret to the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, saw its commander Han to plot, and with five hundred soldiers of the guard followed him; mingling with the Control Crane guards, they entered.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yougui changed clothes, stole to the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, and plotted with its commander Han; five hundred guardsmen followed him in, mixed with the Control Crane corps, and entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 夜三鼓，斬關入萬春門，至寢中，侍疾者皆走。

translations.literal: At the third watch they cut through the gate into Wanchun Gate, reached the bedchamber, and the attendants all fled.
translations.idiomatic: At the third watch they forced Wanchun Gate and burst into the sleeping quarters; the nurses scattered.

sentences.zh: 太祖惶駭起呼曰：「我疑此賊久矣，恨不早殺之，逆賊忍殺父乎！

translations.literal: Taizu started up in terror and cried: “I have suspected this villain long—I regret I did not kill him sooner! Villain, can you bear to kill your father!
translations.idiomatic: Taizu leapt up in terror and shouted: “I have long known you for a traitor—why did I not kill you sooner! Beast—would you murder your own father!

sentences.zh: 」友珪親吏馮廷諤以劍犯太祖，太祖旋柱而走，劍擊柱者三，太祖憊，仆於床，廷諤以劍中之，洞其腹，腸胃皆流。

translations.literal: ” Yougui’s personal officer Feng Ting’e advanced with a sword against Taizu; Taizu ran around a pillar; the sword struck the pillar three times; Taizu was exhausted and fell on the bed; Ting’e thrust and pierced his belly, and bowels spilled out.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yougui’s henchman Feng Ting’e ran him through with a sword; Taizu circled a pillar while the blade bit the wood three times, then collapsed on the bed. Feng drove the point into his belly and spilled his guts.

sentences.zh: 友珪以裀褥裹之寢中，秘喪四日。

translations.literal: Yougui wrapped him in bedding in the chamber and concealed the death for four days.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui swaddled the corpse in the bedchamber and hid the death for four days.

sentences.zh: 乃出府庫，大賫群臣及諸軍。

translations.literal: Then he opened the treasury and gave great rewards to the ministers and the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Then he opened the vaults and lavished gifts on court and camp.

sentences.zh: 遣受旨丁昭浦矯詔馳至東都，殺友文。

translations.literal: He sent edict-bearer Ding Zhaopu with a forged edict galloping to the eastern capital to kill Youwen.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Ding Zhaopu with a forged edict to the eastern capital to kill Youwen.

sentences.zh: 又下詔曰：「朕艱難創業，逾三十年。

translations.literal: He also issued an edict saying: “I toiled to found the enterprise for more than thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: He also proclaimed: “I founded this house through thirty years of hardship.

sentences.zh: 托於人上，忽焉六載，中外協力，期於小康。

translations.literal: Entrusted upon the throne, suddenly six years have passed; within and without have cooperated, hoping for modest peace.
translations.idiomatic: Six years on the throne, court and camp alike have labored toward a modest peace.

sentences.zh: 豈意友文陰畜異圖，將行大逆。

translations.literal: Who would have thought Youwen secretly harbored alien designs and was about to commit great treason!
translations.idiomatic: Who dreamed that Youwen was plotting treason and preparing a coup!

sentences.zh: 昨二日夜，甲士突入大內，賴友珪忠孝，領兵剿戮，保全朕躬。

translations.literal: On the second night past, armored men burst into the inner palace; thanks to Yougui’s loyalty in leading troops to slaughter them, my person was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Two nights ago armored rebels broke into the inner palace; only Yougui’s loyal sword saved me.

sentences.zh: 然而疾恙震驚，彌所危殆。

translations.literal: Yet the shock of illness leaves me increasingly in peril.
translations.idiomatic: The shock has left me gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 友珪克平兇逆，厥功靡倫，宜委權主軍國。

translations.literal: Yougui quelled the villains; his merit is unmatched—he ought to be entrusted with authority over army and state.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui crushed the traitors; none equals his service. Let him rule army and state.

sentences.zh: 」然後發喪。

translations.literal: ” Only then was mourning announced.
translations.idiomatic: ” Only then was the death made public.

sentences.zh: 乾化二年六月既望，友珪於柩前即皇帝位，拜韓忠武軍節度使，以末帝為汴州留後，河中朱友謙為中書令。

translations.literal: On the full moon of the sixth month of the second year of Qianhua, Yougui took the throne before the coffin; he enfeoffed Han as military governor of Zhongwu, made the Last Emperor acting governor of Bian, and appointed Zhu Youqian of Hezhong Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: On the full moon of the sixth month of Qianhua 2, Yougui was enthroned before the bier; Han became military governor of Zhongwu, the Last Emperor was left as acting governor of Bian, and Zhu Youqian of Hezhong was named Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 友謙不受命。

translations.literal: Youqian did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Youqian refused the post.

sentences.zh: 而懷州龍驤軍三千，劫其將劉重霸，據懷州，自言討賊。

translations.literal: Meanwhile three thousand men of the Dragon Surging Army at Huai seized their commander Liu Chongba, held Huai, and declared themselves punishing the traitor.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile three thousand Dragon Surging troops at Huai seized their commander Liu Chongba, occupied the city, and proclaimed a crusade against the regicide.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，友珪祀天於洛陽南郊，改元曰鳳歷。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, Yougui sacrificed to Heaven at the southern suburbs of Luoyang and changed the era name to Fengli.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of his third year Yougui offered to Heaven at Luoyang’s southern altar and proclaimed the era Fengli.

sentences.zh: 太祖外孫袁象先與駙馬都尉趙巖等，謀與末帝討賊。

translations.literal: Taizu’s maternal grandson Yuan Xiangxian, together with the imperial son-in-law Zhao Yan and others, plotted with the Last Emperor to punish the traitor.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu’s grandson by a daughter, Yuan Xiangxian, joined the imperial son-in-law Zhao Yan and others in a pact with the Last Emperor to overthrow the usurper.

sentences.zh: 二月，象先以禁兵入宮，友珪與妻張氏趨北垣樓下，將逾城以走，不果，使馮廷諤進刃其妻及己，廷諤亦自殺。

translations.literal: In the second month, Xiangxian led the palace guard into the palace; Yougui and his wife Zhang rushed to the foot of the north wall tower, tried to climb the wall and flee, but could not; he had Feng Ting’e advance his blade against his wife and himself; Ting’e also killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Xiangxian entered with the guard; Yougui and Zhang fled to the north wall and tried to scale it in vain. He ordered Feng Ting’e to kill them both; Feng then took his own life.

sentences.zh: 末帝即位，復友文官爵，廢友珪為庶人。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, he restored Youwen’s titles and demoted Yougui to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor restored Youwen’s honors and struck Yougui down to commoner rank.

sentences.zh: 子康王友孜

translations.literal: Son: Youzi, Prince of Kang
translations.idiomatic: Son: Youzi, Prince of Kang

sentences.zh: 康王友孜，目重瞳子，嘗竊自負，以為當為天子。

translations.literal: Youzi, Prince of Kang, had double pupils; he once secretly prided himself on thinking he ought to be emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Youzi, Prince of Kang, had double pupils and secretly believed the throne was his by right.

sentences.zh: 貞明元年，末帝德妃薨，將葬，友孜使刺客夜入寢中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenming, when the Last Emperor’s Virtuous Consort died and was about to be buried, Youzi sent an assassin by night into the bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming 1, as the Virtuous Consort was being readied for burial, Youzi sent a killer into the imperial bedchamber by night.

sentences.zh: 末帝方寐，夢人害己，既寤，聞榻上寶劍槍然有聲，躍起，抽劍曰：「將有變邪！

translations.literal: The Last Emperor was asleep; he dreamed someone meant to harm him; once awake he heard the treasured sword on the couch ring sharply; he leaped up, drew the sword, and said: “Is revolt at hand!
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor slept and dreamed of murder; waking, he heard his sword clatter on the couch-rail. He sprang up, blade in hand: “Treason!

sentences.zh: 」乃索寢中，得刺客，手殺之，遂誅友孜。

translations.literal: ” He then searched the bedchamber, seized the assassin, killed him with his own hand, and then executed Youzi.
translations.idiomatic: ” He searched the room, caught the assassin, slew him himself, and then put Youzi to death.

sentences.zh: 明日，謂趙巖、張漢傑曰：「幾與卿輩不相見。

translations.literal: The next day he said to Zhao Yan and Zhang Hanjie: “I nearly never saw you again.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he told Zhao Yan and Zhang Hanjie: “I almost never saw you again.

sentences.zh: 」由此遂疏弱宗室，而信任趙、張，以至於敗亡。

translations.literal: ” From this he grew distant toward the weakened imperial clan and trusted Zhao and Zhang, until defeat and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: ” From then on he estranged the imperial clan and put his faith in Zhao and Zhang—on the road to ruin.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，《春秋》之法，是非與奪之際，難矣哉！

translations.literal: Alas! The method of the Spring and Autumn Annals—at the juncture of judging right and wrong and bestowing or withholding titles, how hard it is!
translations.idiomatic: Alas! In the Spring and Autumn manner, to judge right from wrong and grant or deny a place in the record—how difficult that is!

sentences.zh: 或問：「梁太祖以臣弒君，友珪以子弒父，一也。

translations.literal: Someone asked: “Liang Taizu as a minister murdered his lord, and Yougui as a son murdered his father—one and the same.
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked: “Taizu of Liang slew his sovereign as a subject; Yougui slew his father as a son—the same crime.

sentences.zh: 與弒即位，逾年改元，《春秋》之法，皆以君書，而友珪不得列於本紀，何也？

translations.literal: The regicide who took the throne changed the era name after a year; by the Spring and Autumn method both are entered as lords—yet Yougui is not placed in the Basic Annals. Why?
translations.idiomatic: A usurper who reigns a year and changes the era is still written as “lord” in the Spring and Autumn—but Yougui is denied a place in the Basic Annals. Why?

sentences.zh: 且父子之惡均，而奪其子，是與其父也，豈《春秋》之旨哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, father and son were equally wicked, yet you strip the son while affirming the father—is that the intent of the Spring and Autumn?
translations.idiomatic: Father and son were equally vile; you erase the son but keep the father—can that be what the Spring and Autumn intended?

sentences.zh: 」予應之曰：「梁事著矣！

translations.literal: ” I answered: “Liang’s affairs are plain enough!
translations.idiomatic: ” I replied: “The Liang story is clear enough!

sentences.zh: 其父之惡，不待與奪其子而後彰，然末帝之志，不可以不伸也。

translations.literal: The father’s wickedness needs no stripping the son’s title to be revealed; yet the Last Emperor’s intent cannot go unvindicated.
translations.idiomatic: The father’s guilt needs no denial of the son’s reign to expose it; but the Last Emperor’s purpose must be honored.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之法，君弒而賊不討者，國之臣子任其責。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn method says: when a lord is murdered and the killer is not punished, the state’s ministers and sons bear the blame.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn rule is this: when a ruler is murdered and the assassin goes unpunished, the guilt falls on the court and the clan.

sentences.zh: 予於友珪之事，所以伸討賊者之志也。」

translations.literal: In my treatment of Yougui’s affair, my purpose is to vindicate the will to punish the traitor.”
translations.idiomatic: In what I write of Yougui, I mean to vindicate the will to punish the regicide.”
